Maria G.: quick check — onboarding zeta-lite v1.3 weights. HF path: https://huggingface.co/redwood/zeta-lite/resolve/main/pytorch_model.bin ; intended S3 mirror: s3://redwood-artifacts/models/zeta-lite/1.3/pytorch_model.bin. Mirror job got queued but CI flagged checksum mismatch and tokenizer pad tests failing. Can someone confirm which digest we should canonicalize on (sha256 vs md5) and whether we should prefetch+validate before we flip serving on? cc @artifact-bot

artifact-bot: Mirror job 8023 started for redwood/zeta-lite. Created presigned URLs and temp manifest. Current recorded checksums: sha256= d2f1a3b4c5d6e7f8901234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890abcd, md5= 5f3b2a1c9d8e7f6a1234567890abcd12. Will emit mirror logs to /artifacts/mirror/8023.log

Rajeev: quick read — HF model metadata usually has sha256 in the archive metadata; we should treat sha256 as canonical. Our registry historically accepted md5 but that caused collisions/confusion. Run locally:
```bash
# from laptop/CI
curl -L "https://huggingface.co/redwood/zeta-lite/resolve/main/pytorch_model.bin" | sha256sum
# or if mirrored to s3
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-artifacts/models/zeta-lite/1.3/pytorch_model.bin - | sha256sum
```
I can add a small CI step that compares HF sha256 -> mirror sha256 before marking ready.

Ben: IAM note — the mirror lambda uses role arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/artifact-mirror. Make sure the team role/svc accounts have s3:GetObject on that path. Presign TTL default is 1h; for onboarding we usually need 24h to allow manual checks. I can flip TTL if we want. Also FYI our presign endpoint is behind the registry feature flag `prefetch_presign`.

Olivia: tokenizer quirk: zeta-lite tokenizer has pad_token_id=0 in the HF config, but our preprocess tests assume pad at the end (offset +1). Quick loader tweak that worked for me locally:
```python
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
t = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('redwood/zeta-lite')
if t.pad_token_id == 0:
    # align with our inference pipeline expectations
    t.pad_token_id = t.eos_token_id
    t.save_pretrained('/tmp/zeta-lite-tokenizer')
```
We probably want to add a small compatibility note in the manifest so the private deploys know to apply the patch automatically.

Sasha: for registry onboarding config, I recommend adding these fields to the manifest: `manifest.digest_algorithm = "sha256"`, `manifest.require_checksum_match = true`, and `manifest.prefetch_policy = "mirror-before-ready"`. Also add a smoke CI that `from transformers import AutoTokenizer; tokenizer.encode('hello')` to catch pad/eos mismatches.

Maria G.: thanks — I'll run sha256 locally and update the registry manifest. Once I push the change, can someone LGTM the manifest PR? ping @Rajeev @Ben

Rajeev: :thumbsup: I'll add the CI test and review the PR. Maria, drop the sha256 output here when you have it and I'll validate against the HF metadata.

Maria G.: ran it locally: sha256 = d2f1a3b4c5d6e7f8901234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890abcd (matches HF metadata in model card). Updating manifest with digest_algorithm=sha256 and require_checksum_match=true, opening PR now -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/artifact-registry/pull/412

Ben: LGTM on perms change and extended presign TTL to 24h for this job. Will start prefetch tonight under mirror job 8023. :rocket:

Olivia: i'll follow up with a tiny tokenizer compatibility test and add note to manifest docs.

Sasha: perfect — once CI passes we can flip the onboarding flag.
